note: City and county income taxes charged on top of the state rate. Only states confirmed against a primary source are listed.

states.name: New York
states.lead: Two places in New York charge income tax of their own on top of the state's, and both come out of the same paycheck.

items.text: City income tax is withheld from people who live in the city, using New York City's own withholding tables for 2026. A bonus paid separately is withheld at the city supplemental rate of 4.25%.

Residents pay a surcharge on top of their state tax, withheld with the city's own tables - supplemental pay at 1.95975%. People who work in Yonkers but live elsewhere pay the nonresident earnings tax of 0.50% of wages instead.

sources.label: NYS-50-T-NYC, New York City withholding tables (1/26)

states.name: Pennsylvania
states.lead: Philadelphia charges a wage tax of its own, and it dwarfs the state's flat rate.

items.text: 3.735% for residents of the city and 3.425% for everyone else who works in it, effective 1 July 2026 - more than the state's own 3.07% either way.

sources.label: City of Philadelphia, Wage Tax rates

states.name: Indiana
states.lead: Every Indiana county charges income tax of its own on top of the state's 2.95%, so nobody in Indiana pays only the state rate.

items.text: County rates run from 0.50% to 3.00% for 2026. Marion County, which is Indianapolis, takes 2.02%.
The county you lived in on 1 January decides it. If you did not live in Indiana on that date, it is the county where you mainly work.

sources.label: Indiana DOR, Departmental Notice #1, effective 1 January 2026

states.name: Maryland
states.lead: Maryland's local tax is not separate from your paycheck - it is withheld alongside the state tax, and it is the reason Maryland withholding looks high.

items.text: Local rates run from 2.25% to 3.30% for 2026, and the rate follows where you live, not where you work. Anne Arundel and Frederick counties charge different rates at different income levels.
The calculator uses 3.20%, near the top of that range. In a county that charges less, your take-home is higher than shown by up to about 1% of your taxable pay.

sources.label: Maryland Comptroller, employer withholding guide, January 2026
Maryland Comptroller, income tax rates and brackets

states.name: Oregon
states.lead: Oregon has one small tax that reaches every worker and two larger ones around Portland that only reach higher earners.

items.text: The statewide transit tax takes 0.1% of wages - from residents wherever they work, and from everyone else for work done in Oregon. It is already included in the figures above.
The supportive housing services tax is 1% of taxable income above $125,000 for a single filer or $200,000 for joint filers. From the 2026 tax year those thresholds rise with inflation.
Preschool for All takes 1.5% of taxable income above $125,000 single or $200,000 joint, and another 1.5% above $250,000 single or $400,000 joint. The rate goes up by 0.8% in 2028.

sources.label: Oregon Department of Revenue, statewide transit tax
City of Portland Revenue Division, Metro SHS and Multnomah PFA personal income tax
